from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Rates of Change", [
            "A derivative is a function's instantaneous slope.",
            "Think of it as velocity from position.",
            "Watch the tangent line slide along the curve."
        ])

        # Assets
        car = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png")
        odometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/odometer.svg")
        
        # Plot Setup
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-1, 3], x_length=3, y_length=2)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2 + 0.5, color=WHITE)
        curve_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        
        # Positioning curve
        self.place_in_area(curve_group, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Positioning car asset
        self.place_at_grid(car, 'A2', scale_factor=0.3)

        # Dynamic objects
        point = ValueTracker(-1.2)
        dot = Dot(color=RED)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(point.get_value(), point.get_value()**2 + 0.5)))
        
        tangent = TangentLine(curve, alpha=0.2, length=1.0, color=RED)
        tangent.add_updater(lambda t: t.become(TangentLine(curve, alpha=(point.get_value()+2)/4, length=1.0, color=RED)))
        
        slope_label = MathTex(f"f'(x)", color=GREEN).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(odometer, 'D5', scale_factor=0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(car))
        self.add(dot, tangent)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(point.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_label), FadeIn(odometer))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Integration as Accumulation", [
            "Integration measures the total area under a curve.",
            "Visualize this as summing infinite thin rectangles.",
            "Bar graphs transform into a smooth curve."
        ])
        
        # Create axes and function
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        func = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.5 * t + 0.5, color=WHITE)

        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        func.match_y(axes)
        
        # Asset for sweeping bar
        sweeping_bar = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bar.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(sweeping_bar, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        sweeping_bar.set_opacity(0)
        self.add(sweeping_bar)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        area = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[0, 4], color="#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(func), FadeIn(area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Visualizing summing rectangles
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(func, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Use the asset to sweep across the area
        self.play(
            FadeOut(area), 
            FadeIn(sweeping_bar.set_opacity(1)),
            Create(rects),
            sweeping_bar.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Transforming to curve
        smooth_area = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[0, 4], color="#FF00FF", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweeping_bar), ReplacementTransform(rects, smooth_area))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Fundamental Theorem: The Inverse Connection",
            ["Integration and differentiation are inverse operations.", 
             "Accumulating the rate recovers the original state.", 
             "Think of them as Undo and Redo."]
        )
        
        # Define mobjects
        integral_expr = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{x} f(t) \, dt", font_size=48)
        derivative_op = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", font_size=48, color=YELLOW)
        final_result = MathTex(r"f(x)", font_size=48, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Asset Loading
        undo_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/undo.svg")
        redo_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/redo.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(integral_expr, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(integral_expr))
        self.place_at_grid(undo_icon, 'A6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(undo_icon))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        derivative_op.next_to(integral_expr, LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(derivative_op))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        equals = MathTex("=", font_size=48)
        equals.next_to(integral_expr, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        final_result.next_to(equals, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(redo_icon, 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(equals), Write(final_result), FadeIn(redo_icon))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)", [
            "The derivative of the area function is f(x).",
            "A vertical line sweeps across the area.",
            "Area growth matches the sprayer's width.",
            "This proves the fundamental connection.",
            "We relate rate of change to accumulation."
        ])
        
        # Setup Axes and Functions
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        f = lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 2)**2 + 1
        graph = axes.plot(f, color=BLUE)
        
        # Area representation
        area = axes.get_area(graph, x_range=[0, 3], color=GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        
        # Place graph area
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(graph, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(area, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Sweeping line
        line = Line(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(0, 3), color=RED).scale(0.5).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 1.5))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(graph), Create(axes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Rates of Change
sections.content: Briefly define a derivative as the instantaneous slope of a function (velocity from position). Visually represent this as a tangent line sliding along a curve.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing prey: The derivative represents the cheetah's instantaneous speed at any point in time.

sections.title: Visualizing Integration as Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the integral as the 'area under the curve.' Use a 'filling' animation where a bar graph transforms into a smooth curve, showing the summation of infinite thin rectangles.
sections.example: The cheetah's GPS tracker logging total distance covered by summing up small 'snapshots' of velocity over time.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Inverse Connection
sections.content: Explain that integration is the reverse operation of differentiation. If you accumulate the 'rate of change,' you recover the 'original state.' Use a 'Undo/Redo' button metaphor.
sections.example: If the speedometer records velocity (derivative), integrating that data perfectly reconstructs the odometer reading (position).

sections.title: Key Concept: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
sections.content: Present the visual proof: The rate of change of the area function F(x) is exactly the height of the curve f(x). Show a moving vertical line that 'sweeps' out area.
sections.example: A robotic arm painting a wall: The rate at which paint covers the wall (area growth) equals the width of the sprayer at that exact point.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the concepts. Derivatives 'break down' curves into slopes; Integrals 'build up' curves into areas. They are two sides of the same coin.
sections.example: A digital music synthesizer: Differentiating the waveform changes its pitch (slope), while integrating it modifies its volume/energy (accumulation).
